prompt.context: Our client, Alpha Auto, is a large US-based auto manufacturer that produces a broad range of vehicles from compact cars to medium-sized commercial trucks. Alpha Auto emerged from bankruptcy in 2009 and its share in the US auto market has declined from 11.2% to 9.5% over the past 3 years. With increasing consumer interest in electric vehicles, Alpha Auto wants to evaluate the option of expanding its product range to offer an electric or hybrid vehicle.
prompt.question: The client wants our advice on how to evaluate this option. Should Alpha Auto enter the electric vehicle market, and if so, which segment should they target, at what price, and using which production approach?

clarifying_info.q: What is Alpha Auto's current financial health?
clarifying_info.a: Net income in 2014 was $1.2 billion. Cash at year-end was $8.4 billion.

clarifying_info.q: What brands and products does Alpha Auto currently sell?
clarifying_info.a: Three brands: Astra (low-to-medium end luxury sedans, convertibles, minivans), Neptune (low-end passenger, performance cars, crossovers, SUVs), and Forge (trucks and commercial vehicles).

clarifying_info.q: Does Alpha Auto have the technology to manufacture electric or hybrid vehicles?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. R&D has developed technology to manufacture electric/hybrid powertrains and they have commitments from battery suppliers for batteries at all capacities.

clarifying_info.q: How does Alpha Auto distribute its vehicles?
clarifying_info.a: Through a network of dealerships across the US.

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of the US auto market?
clarifying_info.a: Total units sold in the US in 2014: 8 million. Electric vehicles represent 1.5% of total units. Average price of a vehicle in the US is $33,560; average price of an electric vehicle is $40,025.

clarifying_info.q: What is the growth outlook for the electric vehicle market?
clarifying_info.a: See Exhibit 1 for the EV unit sales forecast 2015-2020 (assumes oil at $100/barrel and charging station network continues expanding at current rate).

clarifying_info.q: What are the EV market segments?
Who are the competitors in the EV market?
clarifying_info.a: See Exhibit 5 for market share data.

clarifying_info.q: Are segment share percentages expected to change in the future?
clarifying_info.a: No, assume segment percentages remain constant.

clarifying_info.q: What happens if oil prices fall below $100/barrel?
clarifying_info.a: Some decrease in EV demand is expected.

exhibits.title: Electric Vehicle Unit Sales Forecast, US, 2015-2020
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing forecasted annual EV unit sales in the US from 2015 to 2020, with assumptions of oil prices at $100/barrel and continued expansion of charging station network.

exhibits.title: Electric Vehicle Segments
exhibits.shows: A table listing three EV segments (Economy, Luxury, Sports) with average prices and share of EV market in 2014.

exhibits.title: Segment Pricing and Market Share Capture Options
exhibits.shows: A matrix showing two pricing strategies (high pricing vs. low pricing) with the market share within segment Alpha Auto could capture at each price point, across the three EV segments.

exhibits.title: Production Facility Options
exhibits.shows: Two production options: Option 1 (retrofit existing facility) and Option 2 (new facility), each with investment cost, max annual capacity, production start date, and average unit costs by segment.

exhibits.title: Electric Vehicle Market Share, US, 2014
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing market share of EV manufacturers in the US in 2014.

framework: Market attractiveness: size, growth trajectory, risks to forecast (oil prices, charging infrastructure)
Competitive landscape: existing players, market share concentration, Alpha Auto's differentiation opportunity
Segment selection: fit with brand/positioning, price elasticity, competitor concentration, profitability by segment
Pricing strategy: high vs. low price and implied unit volume and revenue by segment
Production / operations: build vs. retrofit, capital requirements, unit costs, max capacity, ROIC
Financial assessment: revenue, gross profit, OPEX, net income, ROIC for each option
Recommendation: segment, price, production option, rationale, risks, next steps

questions.prompt: What is the size and growth outlook of the EV market, and what risks should Alpha Auto consider?
questions.guidance: The EV market in 2014 is ~120,000 units (1.5% of 8M). Exhibit 1 shows rapid growth to 400K by 2018 and 800K by 2020. Candidate should flag that the EV market, while growing fast, is still a small fraction of total auto sales. Risks include lower oil prices dampening demand and uncertainty in charging infrastructure expansion. A strong candidate proactively acknowledges these growth assumptions are conditional.

questions.prompt: What factors should Alpha Auto consider when selecting a target EV segment (Economy, Luxury, or Sports)?
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover: segment growth (all grow proportionally), profitability (higher price = higher margin), price elasticity, competitor concentration, fit with Alpha Auto's current brand and positioning, manufacturing capabilities, and distribution. Alpha Auto's brands (Astra, Neptune, Forge) skew toward lower-to-mid-end — this is a strong signal toward the Economy segment. Sports has only 1% of EV volume — too small. Luxury is viable but brand fit is weaker.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, which segment and price point would you recommend for Alpha Auto? Calculate expected unit sales.
questions.guidance: Candidate should pick a forecast year from 2018-2020 (production cannot start until 2018). Economy + low pricing ($30,000, 10% share within segment) is the recommended answer. Example using 2018: Total EV = 400,000; Economy = 400,000 x 75% = 300,000; Alpha Auto units = 300,000 x 10% = 30,000. Sports segment should be eliminated due to poor brand fit and tiny volume. Candidate may run partial calculations across segments to compare.

math.setup: Total forecast EV units (2018) x Economy segment share x Alpha Auto market share within Economy at low price
steps: Alpha Auto units at low pricing (10% share within segment) = 300,000 x 10% = 30,000
Alpha Auto units at high pricing (5% share within segment) = 300,000 x 5% = 15,000
math.answer: 30,000 units at low price ($30,000); 15,000 units at high price ($32,000)

questions.prompt: Alpha Auto has two production options (Exhibit 4). Which would you recommend? Calculate ROIC for your chosen segment and pricing.
questions.guidance: Candidate should first discuss qualitative factors: Option 1 lowers capital exposure if EV growth disappoints; Option 2 provides scale and lower unit costs. Then calculate ROIC. For Economy segment + low pricing + Option 1 (recommended): Revenue = 30,000 x $30,000 = $900M; Gross profit = $900M - (30,000 x $24,000 unit cost) = $900M - $720M = $180M; OPEX = 5% x $900M = $45M; Net income = $180M - $45M = $135M; ROIC = $135M / $1B = 13.5%. For Option 2: same revenue/gross profit but investment = $3B, so ROIC = $195M / $3B = 6.5%. Option 1 yields higher ROIC (13.5% vs 6.5%). Candidate should flag OPEX = 5% of sales applies to both options equally.

math.setup: Revenue = units x price; Gross profit = Revenue - (units x unit cost); OPEX = 5% x Revenue; Net Income = Gross profit - OPEX; ROIC = Net Income / Investment
math.answer: Option 1 ROIC = 13.5%; Option 2 ROIC = 6.5%. Option 1 recommended on ROIC basis.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors should Alpha Auto consider in selecting the target EV segment?

categories.name: Brand & Positioning Fit
ideas: Alpha Auto brands (Astra, Neptune, Forge) skew lower-to-mid end — matches Economy segment
Entry into Luxury or Sports would require significant brand repositioning
Consumer perception post-bankruptcy may limit premium pricing credibility

categories.name: Market Size & Growth
ideas: Economy is 75% of EV market — largest volume opportunity
Sports is only 1% of EV market — insufficient scale
All segments grow proportionally under constant share assumption

categories.name: Profitability & Pricing
ideas: Higher-priced segments (Luxury, Sports) offer better margin per unit
Economy low-price strategy captures more volume, compensating lower unit margin
Price elasticity likely higher in Economy segment — lowering price meaningfully increases share

categories.name: Competitive Dynamics
ideas: Economy segment may have more room for a cost-competitive new entrant
Sports segment dominated by performance-oriented brands — difficult to compete

categories.name: Manufacturing & Operations
ideas: Economy segment unit costs ($24K Option 1, $22K Option 2) well below price — strong margin
Capacity constraints favor Economy given larger volume is achievable within 60K cap
Distribution network of dealerships well-suited to volume Economy sales

recommendation: Alpha Auto should enter the electric vehicle market targeting the Economy segment at a low price of $30,000, capturing an estimated 10% market share within that segment
Retrofit the existing production facility (Option 1, $1B investment) to begin production in 2018, yielding an estimated ROIC of 13.5% in the first production year
risks: Actual EV market growth may fall short of forecasts, particularly if oil prices decline significantly
Competitors may respond with price cuts, compressing Alpha Auto's margins in the Economy segment
Technological advances by competitors (e.g., longer range, faster charging) could erode Alpha Auto's product competitiveness
Government tax incentives for EVs may change, affecting consumer demand
next_steps: Finalize engineering and supplier contracts for Economy-segment electric powertrain
Execute retrofit of existing production facility and plan for 2018 production launch
Develop go-to-market and dealer network activation plan for the new EV lineup
Monitor oil price trends and competitor pricing closely to adjust strategy as needed
Assess option to expand into Luxury segment once Economy foothold is established
